description: A pure CALCULATION node — name each connected component of a graph from a labels array, and optionally stamp an edge type and thickness at the same time. Graph in, graph out; draws nothing on canvas.
instructions:
A value-only node: it takes a GRAPH as JSON plus a LABELS array, and returns the same graph with `label` stamped on every edge — the name of the component that edge belongs to. It has no geometry input or output and draws nothing.

WHY IT EXISTS: Set Thickness gives a whole graph ONE type and width, which answers "what kind of thing is this". It cannot answer "which one is it". Object Detection publishes `val-graph` (one closed ring per detected object, in detection order) alongside `val-labels` (the names, same order) — wire both in here and component i takes label i, so a graph of six rectangles becomes "Bedroom", "Bathroom", "sofa", … Together with `type` and `thickness` this turns a raw detection into a fully tagged family in one node.

INPUT: graph takes { "nodes": [{ "id", "x", "y" }, ...], "edges": [{ "from_node_id", "to_node_id" }, ...] } — coordinates in metres, local to the anchor. Wire Object Detection val-graph, or any other graph node's val-graph, into valin-graph.

LABELS accepts a JSON array of strings ("[\"Bedroom\",\"Kitchen\"]") or a bare comma-separated list typed into the field. Components are numbered by the order their first node appears, which is the order the boxes were serialised — that is what keeps label i on box i. A SINGLE label names EVERY component, which is what you want when the whole graph is one family (all walls). A component past the end of the array keeps whatever label it already had.

EDGE TYPE stamps `type` on every edge — "wall", "door", "window", "room", "furniture" or "opening". THICKNESS overwrites `thickness` in metres; leave it at 0 to keep whatever the incoming edges already carry (a detection graph has none, a wall graph usually does).

OUTPUT: val-graph publishes the tagged graph — wire it into Merge Graph to union it with the other families, each keeping its own type, width and label. `val-labelled` reports how many edges actually received a name, which is how you catch a labels array that was shorter than the component count.

Every parameter is wireable (valin-*).
